extraction.name: Microsoft Common Objects in Context (MS COCO)
extraction.description: A large-scale, richly annotated dataset of complex everyday scenes containing common objects in their natural context. It includes instance-level segmentations and labels 91 common object categories with 2,500,000 labeled instances in 328,000 images.
extraction.creator: Tsung-Yi Lin; Michael Maire; Serge Belongie; Lubomir Bourdev; Ross Girshick; James Hays; Pietro Perona; Deva Ramanan; C. Lawrence Zitnick; Piotr Dollár
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were collected from Flickr by searching for pairs of object categories or object-scene category pairs, then filtered via Amazon Mechanical Turk to remove invalid or iconic images. Additional AMT interfaces were used for category labeling, instance spotting, instance segmentation, segmentation verification, and crowd labeling.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Candidate Flickr images associated with text captions, gathered through object-object and object-scene search queries.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation involved multiple AMT tasks with task-specific interfaces and instructions: filtering invalid/iconic images, category labeling by dragging category icons onto one instance per present category, and instance spotting by clicking all instances of a given category. Workers were given examples in instructions for the filtering task.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: For category labeling, one instance per object category present in the image needed to be annotated.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The 2014 release is limited to 80 categories, with 11 categories omitted from segmentation due to too many instances, ambiguity/difficulty in labeling, category confusion, or too few instances. Test annotations are not released, and crowd labeling for images with more than ten instances of a category does not identify individual object instances.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes images and annotations of people/person instances, as well as human body parts such as face, hand, eye, mouth, nose, head, hair, arms, legs, ears, elbows, fingers, torso, back, armpits, and feet.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training, validation, and test splits for object detection/segmentation evaluation. Train and validation annotations are released, while test annotations are withheld and evaluated through an automatic evaluation server.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper describes a cumulative 2015 release with expanded train/val/test image counts, notes that some omitted segmentations may be added in that release, and mentions that the evaluation server is being finalized.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were explicitly filtered to remove iconic images when single-category searches were used; category labels were determined with a hierarchical labeling approach, and false positives were handled in subsequent annotation stages.

name.evidence: The Microsoft Common Objects in COntext (MS COCO) dataset

description.evidence: We introduce a large, richly-annotated dataset comprised of images depicting complex everyday scenes of common objects in their natural context... The Microsoft Common Objects in COntext (MS COCO) dataset contains 91 common object categories... In total the dataset has 2,500,000 labeled instances in 328,000 images.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: “Flickr provides a rich image collection associated with text captions... we first collected candidate images by searching for pairs of object categories, or pairs of object and scene categories.”

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: “Only a single instance of each object category needs to be annotated in the image.”

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: “Note that we have limited the 2014 release to a subset of 80 categories. We did not collect segmentations for the following 11 categories: hat, shoe, eyeglasses (too many instances), mirror, window, door, street sign (ambiguous and difficult to label), plate, desk (due to confusion with bowl and dining table, respectively) and blender, hair brush (too few instances).”

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: “There are nearly 270k segmented people” and “person ... face ... hand ... eye ... mouth ... nose ... head ... hair ... arms ... legs ... ears ... elbows ... fingers ... torso ... back ... armpits”

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: “Following established protocol, annotations for train and validation data will be released, but not for test. We are currently finalizing the evaluation server for automatic evaluation on the test set.”

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: “The cumulative 2015 release will contain a total of 165,482 train, 81,208 val, and 81,434 test images.” and “We may add segmentations for some of these categories in the cumulative 2015 release.”

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: "in the rare cases in which enough images could not be found, we searched for single categories and performed an explicit filtering stage to remove iconic images"; "we used a hierarchical approach"; "A category is considered present if any worker indicated the category; false positives are handled in subsequent stages."
